decision: no-go for the $8–12 capture as specified
reasons: Learning showed no value. On the holdout G1 escalated all 30 writes (0/9 approvals saved) against DC's 3/9 and D's 2/9, with 0/21 false allows for all three. Its out-of-fold threshold at the 95% catch target sat at 0.9995. On the revealed stream it saved a median 3 approvals against DC's 7 and D's 12, at 2 false allows (DC 2, D 3). No G1 challenger was ever promoted over 'escalate everything' on the promotion set, in any of 20 orderings.

Shared concepts showed no measurable value over the baseline. DC versus D on the holdout: same false allows (0/21), asks 27/30 against 28/30 (family bootstrap −4 pts, 90% interval −11 to +11). On the promotion set DC had 3/18 false allows where D had 0/18.

Transfer is unmeasured. Only one action (exchange: 10 writes, all should escalate) met the coverage rule, and it has no write that should run. Every other action and the telecom domain are inconclusive.

The one positive signal is adaptation. Revealing real prerequisite failures as corrections raised G1's catches of later prerequisite failures on other actions from 27/59 to 45/59 (summed over 16 usable orderings). It also raised escalations of writes that should run from 145/187 to 162/187. Consent corrections changed nothing, because every arm already caught those failures. The remaining concepts had too few corrections to measure.

A bigger capture of the same design would mostly add more of the same few scenario families: 16 families in all, with 5 in the holdout. Phase 2 should first change what the pilot shows is binding: more families per action rather than more trials, and a G1 threshold procedure that can pass at this data size. That needs its own go/no-go.
